text: Trump pays four dollars a gallon. In Iran, the same gallon costs eleven cents. Here's why.
In America, the price at the pump isn't just gas.
About half of it, fifty-two percent, is the crude oil itself.
Twenty-two percent goes to refining it into gasoline.
Fifteen percent pays for trucks, storage, and the station.
And about twelve percent is taxes. Roughly fifty cents a gallon.
Every step wants its cut, and the price follows the world market.
So in America, oil companies, refiners, stations, and tax collectors all get paid from one gallon.
Now Iran. The government controls the price, and it sets it far below the market.
On average, about eleven cents a gallon. Even the top tier is under twenty.
Part of that is Iran's currency. It lost so much value, prices look tiny in dollars.
But cheap gas has a bill. An Iranian official said importing gasoline costs about one dollar a gallon.
So the state sells it for pennies, and pays the difference.
Cheap fuel means people burn more of it, and some gets smuggled across the border.
That's why Iran has been raising prices in steps. This September, the top tier doubled.
So Americans pay the market price. Iran pays with a subsidy.
Which price is the fair one? Tell me in the comments.
